summary.text: Granite is a coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock made mostly of quartz, alkali feldspar, mica and plagioclase.
It forms from magma rich in silica and alkali metal oxides that cools slowly and turns solid underground, and it is common in Earth's continental crust.
Granite is nearly always massive and tough, which has made it a widespread building stone throughout human history.

items.prompt: Magma with the same makeup as granite erupts at the surface and cools there instead. Which rock forms?
items.explain: Rhyolite is the extrusive, surface-cooled equivalent of granite.

items.prompt: Granite has been chosen for buildings since ancient times. What about the rock made it such a good choice?

options.label: It is light enough to float on water
It dissolves slowly to form a smooth glaze
It is tough and lacks internal weak layers
It is soft enough to carve with bare hands

items.explain: Granite is nearly always massive, lacking internal structures, and tough, and these properties made it a widespread construction stone.

items.prompt: Dry granite melts at well over 1,000 °C. What happens to its melting temperature when water is present under high pressure?
items.explain: Granite's melting temperature is strongly reduced by water, falling as low as 650 °C at a few hundred megapascals of pressure.

items.prompt: Two polished granite countertops come from different quarries: one is pink and the other gray. What most likely explains the difference?

options.label: One was cooled much faster than the other
Their mixes of minerals are different
One was dyed at the stone factory
One has been exposed to more sunlight

items.explain: Granites can be mainly white, pink or gray, depending on the minerals they contain.

items.prompt: Groundwater is moving through a solid granite hillside. Where is most of it able to flow?

options.label: Evenly through tiny pores in the grains
Nowhere, since granite blocks all water
Along cracks and fractures in the rock

items.explain: Granite has poor primary permeability, but water can pass readily through cracks and fractures where they exist.

items.prompt: The word granite comes from a Latin word. What did that word refer to?
items.explain: Granite comes from the Latin granum, a grain, after the coarse-grained structure of this fully crystalline rock.
